notable_absence.finding: The /info example response's collection-level breakdown (per-scope, per-collection mutation and tombstone counts inside an imported repository's backup list) is the single most granular data-shape in this entire batch, yet no page anywhere in this batch's read set links it to the Data Service's own collection/scope model as a monitoring source - it is presented purely as an artifact of the backup archive's own internal bookkeeping. Not asserted as a relation for lack of a fitting predicate beyond the monitoredVia relation already recorded above.

cross_component_finding: Closes out this batch's port-architecture thread (see backup-get-plan-info.json for where it was first raised): both dedicated-port (8097) and proxied-through-cluster-manager (8091, via '_p/backup/') access to the same repository-info data are now attested TWICE each within this eleven-page batch, which raises confidence this is a real, intentional dual-homing rather than a one-off typo in either example. Combined with backup-create-repository.json's and backup-examine-data.json's field-level confirmations (archive/repository containment; the collection-string/data_path addressing match), this batch's overall verdict on the round's core question is: round 11's 'SAME construct' finding for backup:repository holds up strongly and is now confirmed from three independent angles (storage-location semantics, document addressing, and now REST transport architecture) - but the Backup Service layers scheduling (backup:plan), a broader task-type set (BACKUP/MERGE/PRUNE), and lifecycle states with no CLI equivalent (backup:imported-repository) on top of that shared construct, so 'same repository, different surface' is accurate at the storage layer and incomplete as a description of the two surfaces' full capability sets.
